title: Life experiences
source: User-provided workbook photo, manually transcribed; Word File German translations suggested separately

entries.description: To snap a picture that looks just right
To start having strong romantic feelings for sb
To shoot a little movie
To leap from a bridge tied to an elastic rope
To get a trout or salmon out of the water
To start studying Italian or Spanish, for example

entries.english: to spend a weekend on your own
entries.description: To be alone from Saturday to Sunday

entries.english: to have a party for no reason at all
entries.german: ohne jeden Grund eine Party feiern
entries.description: To celebrate with friends when there's nothing to celebrate

entries.english: to try food you never thought you'd eat
entries.german: Essen probieren, von dem du nie gedacht hättest, dass du es isst
entries.description: To taste a dish that seemed too strange or scary before

entries.english: to go a week without using your phone
entries.german: eine Woche lang ohne Handy auskommen
entries.description: To live seven days and never once touch a mobile

entries.example: I've collected stamps since I was 12.
entries.description: To gather things of one kind as a hobby

entries.example: I have added 200 new records to my record collection.
entries.description: Many stamps or records kept together by one person

entries.example: The charity shop had second-hand records for sale.
entries.description: Available to buy

entries.example: You don't see many of those butterflies. They're very rare.
entries.description: Not common; hard to find

entries.example: Good point. Maybe I should start learning Italian.
entries.description: You say this when sb has made a clever remark

entries.example: You're a good photographer. I'm not - I'm rubbish at taking photos.
entries.description: To be really bad at doing sth

entries.example: I did 30 press-ups yesterday. My arms are aching.
entries.description: To hurt for a long time, e.g. your head or tooth

entries.example: The principal will announce the winners of the science fair in the afternoon.
entries.description: To tell people sth officially

entries.example: When he finished, he begged again for no more new followers.
entries.description: To ask for sth again and again in a desperate way

entries.example: After a long day of hiking, Maria felt completely exhausted.
entries.description: Very, very tired

entries.example: To keep fit, Sandra goes for a run every morning.
entries.description: To stay healthy by doing sport

entries.example: Harry posted a video of him doing 35 press-ups.
entries.description: Exercise: push your body away from the floor with your arms

entries.example: After the workout, my arms and shoulders were sore.
entries.description: Painful, e.g. muscles after a workout

entries.example: After hours of dancing at the party, everyone was sweating.
entries.description: To get wet skin when you're hot or working hard

entries.example: I bought this painting at an auction.
entries.description: A sale where people bid and the highest offer wins

entries.example: The building went up in flames and burnt to the ground.
entries.description: To be completely destroyed by fire

entries.example: People believed that this was the only copy of the book left.
entries.description: One of many printed books with the same title

entries.example: After the trial, the murderer was executed.
entries.description: To kill sb as a legal punishment

entries.example: Don Vicente was fascinated with books.
entries.description: Extremely interested in sth

entries.example: I'm furious that I wasn't told about it.
entries.description: Very, very angry

entries.example: The judge sentenced him to five years in prison.
entries.description: The person who decides in a court of law

entries.example: She works in the town library as a librarian.
entries.description: Sb whose job is to look after books others can borrow

entries.example: I never buy books; I always go to the library.
entries.description: A place where you can borrow books

entries.example: The monks lived in a big monastery outside the city.
entries.description: A building where a religious group of men live

entries.example: A monk is a member of a religious group of men.
entries.description: A man who lives a simple life of prayer with other men

entries.example: He said that he had nothing to do with the murders.
entries.description: The crime of killing sb on purpose

entries.example: That ring means a lot to me. It's very precious.
entries.description: Very valuable and important to you

entries.example: We need to preserve our traditions and our heritage.
entries.description: To keep sth safe so it lasts

entries.example: He was sentenced to death for his crime.
entries.description: To give sb the punishment of being killed in court

entries.english: I'll make it up to you.
entries.example: I'm sorry for missing your party - I'll make it up to you.
entries.description: You promise this after letting sb down

entries.example: I'm truly sorry that I broke your new record.
entries.description: Really, honestly

entries.example: I'm sorry. Please, don't be too cross.
entries.description: Annoyed; a bit angry

entries.example: I'm sorry, I'm such a fool.
entries.description: A silly or stupid person

entries.example: Are you paying together or separately?
entries.description: Not together; one by one
